gap: No result ChatGPT got states that 'AI bird ID' means four different things across the picks. Birdfy's free tier identifies every visit with no limit. Bird Buddy's free tier is manual only, and automatic ID plus '2K Ultra' video cost $69.99/yr. standout_why: I could not open the two pages ChatGPT cited (wired.com and goodhousekeeping.com both refused the fetch), so this score rests on the top uncited results. feederfield.com (rank 1, 2026-10-07) correctly says Bird Buddy's automatic ID needs a paid plan. It names only Family Premium at $98.99/yr, not the $69.99 Individual plan, and calls Birdfy's AI terms 'unclear' with a 10-per-day free cap. Birdfy's own membership page now says the free tier has unlimited recognition. birdfeederlab.com (rank 3) says Bird Buddy's 'core AI identification is free'. Bird Buddy's own comparison table says free accounts get manual AI+ recognition only, and that 2K Ultra is not in the free tier. Neither page mentions Kiwibit's split into SKUs with and without Lifetime AI, or that its cheaper solar SKU's AI is only a 30-day trial. The idea that subscriptions matter is not new (feederfield covers part of it), which is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: It changes the cost ranking among ChatGPT's picks. Birdfy (Feeder Wood or Feeder with Solar Panel, both $119.99 on birdfy.com) is the only maker in the set confirmed to give unlimited automatic ID on the free tier. Bird Buddy Pro Solar needs $69.99/yr on top of the feeder price to get automatic ID and its top '2K Ultra' video. For Kiwibit, the shopper has to buy the 'Lifetime AI' SKU, $40–60 more, or the ID turns into a subscription after 30 days. ChatGPT's Kiwibit card ($159.99, Chewy) doesn't say which SKU it is. For a shopper who wants a solar feeder with auto-ID and no subscription, this confirms Birdfy and pushes Bird Buddy down.
